event.title: Law Lake tornado: Sentinel-2 canopy change (revised baseline)
event.method: Explicit v2 42-day baseline / unchanged 21-day comparison; distinct-date Sentinel-2 reflectance medians and predeclared NDVI/NBR decline in baseline mapped-tree cover

sources.label: NTP event assessment and explicit Sentinel-2 observability evidence
ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 baseline land cover
Kingfield and de Beurs (2017): tornado spectral response and land-cover/season limitations

limitations: This is satellite-observed spectral change near a documented tornado, not confirmed canopy-loss fraction, treefall, structural damage, wind speed or EF severity.
NDVI/NBR thresholds are predeclared exploratory diagnostics, not scientifically calibrated damage classes. Report all nine sensitivity combinations; never tune to NTP agreement.
2021 WorldCover tree cover can be stale or misclassified in 2025. The baseline NDVI criterion limits the study population, not all forest or all tornado-affected land.

The revised June 15–July 26 42-day baseline is farther from the event and asymmetric with the 21-day comparison. Phenology/leaf development, moisture, illumination, logging, other wind, fire and cloud/shadow can cause change; this is a stronger temporal confound than the failed original 21-day baseline.

Each 20 m cell mixes vegetation and surroundings. RGB/indices are medians of daily observations, not a simultaneous photograph; per-pixel first/last contributing dates and distinct clear-date counts are retained.

The original July 6–26 baseline failed its unchanged 80% mapped-forest coverage requirement (35.959%). V2 is an explicitly documented one-time baseline revision; quality/count/coverage/indicator thresholds are unchanged, and no search or automatic relaxation occurs.

Unobserved or ineligible land is not unchanged or undamaged. Two clear-date and two coverage gates still fail closed; original-window count/support rasters and per-date forest coverage are diagnostic, not evidence that V2 succeeds.
NTP independently documents the event using satellite review including Sentinel imagery. It is contextual corroboration of observability, not independent pixel-level validation of this experiment.

As checked 22 October 2026, NTP's current public Damage Tracks service does not contain a full Law Lake line. Do not synthesize a line or footprint from published start/end coordinates, maximum width or a map image.

revision.reason: Original 21-day baseline had only 35.959124894% qualified mapped-forest coverage; preserve failure, revise baseline once to fixed 42-day window, retaining all quality/count/coverage/indicator thresholds
revision.result_used_for_revision: Observation coverage only, not candidate area or reference agreement

pre.composite: Per-UTC-day mosaic, stable system:index tie order, then bandwise median of distinct daily observations
pre.pixel_dates: first_day/last_day are earliest/latest contributing clear UTC days since 1970-01-01, not a fictitious single median acquisition date

post.composite: Per-UTC-day mosaic, stable system:index tie order, then bandwise median of distinct daily observations
post.pixel_dates: first_day/last_day are earliest/latest contributing clear UTC days since 1970-01-01, not a fictitious single median acquisition date

daily_forest_coverage.scope: Optional per-date area diagnostic retrieval failed; source inventory and analytical date/count/support rasters remain authoritative. No coverage gate or pixel-quality fallback was applied.

forest_source.aggregation: All contributing WorldCover source pixels must map to tree cover on each 20 m target cell

provenance.window_selection: Explicit V2 recipe fixed before its new computation; no automatic date search, reference/candidate-based tuning or subsequent threshold relaxation
